title: Prepare physical-device silent-blocking probes
summary: Common protocol and both host-prepared probes are complete. Stop for device connection; no physical silent-blocking verdict yet.
description:
COMPLETED PREPARATION: T019, T020 and T021 are done. This phase supplies the common physical protocol and minimal installable probes, not production integration or a silent-call acceptance result. Prior P001 capacity/SDK evidence remains preserved.

PROTOCOL: tools/device-tests/README.md and results-template.md define a deliberately missed empty-fixture baseline, ringing controls, repeated denied attempts and recovery in unlocked foreground/background and locked states. Observe sound, vibration, incoming UI, notifications and delayed carrier messages separately. Call records are allowed; the app adds no alert. No voicemail settings or carrier-service changes without consent.

IPHONE: tools/entry-limit-harness/App/App.swift:12, Shared/HarnessConfiguration.swift:59/:113 and CallDir/CallDirectoryHandler.swift:22 support private exact/empty fixtures, real extension status/reload diagnostics and the preserved blocking/identification capacity modes. tools/device-tests/ios-probe.py:100/:143 stages private builds, checks packaged fixtures/versions and separates explicit signing/install. Unsigned empty and synthetic-exact Release iPhoneOS builds plus focused Swift/Python tests passed. These are host artifacts, not device-provisioned apps; the synthetic fixture is not callable. The harness README documents signing/install/enable/reload/clear/cleanup. Production CallDirectoryExtension remains separate and incomplete.

ANDROID: apps/android/app/src/main/java/com/antoniopantano/callerfilter/ScreeningService.kt:13/:33/:66 supplies the protected screening service. MainActivity.kt:17 provides role/fixture/status controls. ProbeEngine.kt:49/:63/:79 uses existing Rust exact matching and a one-response/deadline guard; ProbeStore.kt:32 keeps native initialization/evaluation and preference changes on a serial worker. Deny requests disallow/reject/missed-notification suppression, not silence-only or call-log hiding. Empty/nonmatch/error/deadline paths allow. Diagnostics are redacted and distinguish attempted responses from framework acknowledgement. The configured local watchdog and local-bind timing do not establish the full device deadline.

ANDROID BUILD/EVIDENCE: tools/build-android.sh plus tools/uniffi-android.toml generate fresh Rust libraries and Android-compatible JNA-cleaner bindings. JNA 5.17 and ABI filters provide paired Rust/JNA arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a and x86_64 libraries, with checked 16KB ZIP/ELF64 alignment. tools/device-tests/android-probe.py:76/:116/:157 separates build/verification from explicit-device install/capture. Final development-signed APK: target/device-tests/android/ready-host-synthetic-asgtxqx5/caller-filter-probe.apk; sibling build record/log/manifest/permissions retain evidence. Actual Rust/JNA host cases and packaged input, six final Python tooling/static-guard tests, assembleDebug, Lint (0 errors, 10 non-blocking warnings), signature, inventory/permission/alignment checks and documentation/whitespace checks passed. The APK fixture is synthetic, not callable. android-probe.md documents prerequisites, private real-fixture rebuild, controls and cleanup.

BOUNDARIES: no new matcher or exported Rust API, no national-number guessing and no production editor. Private numbers/device IDs/generated artifacts stay ignored; APK fixture data is not encrypted. Clearing Android deny does not erase its bundled fixture; empty rebuild/uninstall requires consent. iPhone App Groups, paid-team features and production shared storage are not prerequisites. Full UI, national partial-input validation, AND/OR, Contains, geography, OTA, SMS and capacity stress testing are not prerequisites and are not delivered here.

NEXT: no preparation code remains. Stop for the user to connect both phones and authorize device actions. Pairing, trust, iPhone provisioning/extension approval, Android native startup/role grant, real callbacks/reloads/deadlines and physical observations belong to P017/T022–T023. Both probes precede either physical task; those tasks may run in either order and the second consolidates results. No installation, launch, role/extension change or real call has been performed in preparation. Later production integration must repeat accepted cases, and physical verification ends at the user's go/no-go gate.
goals: Have a reproducible protocol and evidence template for no-disturbance blocking on real Android/iOS calls.
Prepare minimal exact-number probes and repeatable build/install instructions without finishing the production apps.
Tell the user when both probes are ready and which pairing, authorization and calling steps require connected hardware.
nonGoals: Physical call execution before the user connects devices.

Existing shared-core exact matcher and P005 generated-binding contract.
T019 protocol before either platform probe; hardware is not needed to declare preparation ready, but device-bound pairing/provisioning remains pending.
risks: Android native SDK/NDK/Gradle packaging may expose failures not covered by host JVM tests.
iOS signing, fixed-device scripts and App Group assumptions could accidentally turn a small probe into production integration.
Silent mode, Focus, other blockers or contact exemptions can create false positive results.
Neither an SDK contract nor a successful build/reload demonstrates absence of real-call alerts.
openQuestions: Which Android handset/OS/carrier and iPhone/iOS/carrier will the user provide? Record when connected rather than guessing.
Which consented caller line(s) and carrier missed-call services will be present during execution?
completionCriteria: T019 protocol and private fixture/evidence handling are documented.
T020 iPhone probe and T021 Android APK build successfully with focused verification and reproducible commands.
Both probes have blocked and allowed/empty controls, visible enablement diagnostics and no custom call notifications.
Preparation-ready report clearly separates checks completed on the host from pairing/permissions/real-call tests still pending; stop and await device connection.

tasks.title: Define the silent-blocking device protocol and evidence matrix
tasks.description:
design-only preparation of the real-device acceptance protocol. No incoming-call behavior has been verified yet: tools/entry-limit-harness/README.md:1 documents entry-capacity measurements, tools/entry-limit-harness/App/App.swift:42 records reload outcomes, and apps/android/app/src/main/java/com/antoniopantano/callerfilter/MainActivity.kt:9 remains a version demo. Read the completed P001/T001 and T002 evidence, but do not promote their SDK/load results to physical call-behavior proof.

DELIVERABLES: add a concise protocol and a reusable result template under tools/device-tests/ (proposed README.md and results-template.md). Describe the minimum builds and exact-number fixture handoff needed by the two sibling preparation tasks. Real numbers, handset identifiers, screenshots and raw logs belong in ignored/local artifacts; committed evidence uses aliases and redaction.

CASES: start with a permitted real cellular call that visibly rings, with Focus/Do Not Disturb, silent mode and other call blockers controlled and recorded. Test one consented, explicitly presented exact caller number with screen locked/unlocked and the probe in foreground/background/not visibly open. Repeat after clearing the block to prove recovery. For Android keep the caller out of contacts unless READ_CONTACTS is deliberately tested; anonymous/withheld calls are not suitable evidence because they never reach screening. Record extension/role state, loaded fixture, build, OS version, handset and carrier for each run.

OUTCOME: blocked calls must not ring, vibrate, show incoming-call UI, or create blocked/missed-call notifications. Call-log entries are acceptable. Observe new and delayed SMS/other unsolicited alerts separately and identify their origin only where evidenced. Carrier services can generate missed-call messages independently; do not assume a message must occur or that the app can disable it. Do not add voicemail settings or require SMS filtering/default-SMS status. Define and record an observation window rather than assuming immediate silence proves no delayed disturbance.

Use pass/fail/blocked/not-tested per case. SDK contracts, simulator runs, host tests and extension-load success cannot replace human observation on real phones. Consent, device connection and any carrier/system changes remain with the user. Produce a readiness checklist before asking the user to connect devices; later production integration must repeat the accepted cases. This task defines the protocol, not the outcome or implementation of either probe.

---
**Completion summary:**
Completed the design-only protocol and evidence template. Added tools/device-tests/README.md:7 (no-disturbance acceptance), :20 (SDK/source facts versus unverified physical behavior), :44 (private canonical fixture/evidence handoff), :69 (bounded T020/T021 deliverables and readiness), :100 (controlled setup and configurable observation windows), :125 (M0 baseline notification control plus S1/S2/S3 allowed/deny/recovery matrix), and :170 (evidence classification, cleanup and user go/no-go). Added tools/device-tests/results-template.md:8 (device/build/permission record), :25 (settings and timing parameters), :50 (13 required call records with the suggested two deny attempts per state, plus optional nonmatching caller N), :79 (per-attempt channels/timing/evidence), :107 (delayed alert log), :118 (verdict/recovery) and :133 (cross-platform review).

Reviewed completed T001/T002 evidence, the current iPhone capacity README/handler/installer/app, Android manifest/native build script, and SDK-36 CallScreeningService lifecycle/builder contracts. Documented that legacy call-log-hiding claims are incorrect for ordinary third-party Android apps; permitted Recents records are not failures. No new global product decision was invented. No-disturbance acceptance, unknown carrier attribution, caller consent and no voicemail/SMS workaround preserve the agreed scope. The deliberately missed M0 control detects globally suppressed notifications; answered A/C controls avoid contaminating deny evidence with additional missed calls. Force-stop/reboot are separate optional lifecycle cases, not disguised background tests.

VERIFICATION: personally reread both new documents and the edited sections. Read-only Python checks passed for all local Markdown links, final newline/trailing whitespace, possible phone/UDID literals, unique M0/S1/S2/S3 case IDs, all 13 required rows initially not-tested, optional N, verdict vocabulary, observation channels and pending user go/no-go. git check-ignore -v confirmed target/device-tests fixture/result paths are ignored; git diff --check passed. No Rust/app build or test suite was run because this task changes documentation only. No physical calls, device installations or silence measurements were performed, and no test result is prefilled as a pass.

REMAINING: none within T019. T020 must implement/build the iPhone probe and T021 the Android probe; the user is asked to connect devices only after both are preparation-ready. T022/T023 still require actual handset/OS/carrier data, consent and real-call evidence. Supplied observation values are configurable test starting points, not measured maximum carrier delays. Source changes in this task are only the two approved Markdown files; existing unrelated work is untouched. No commit or push.

tasks.title: Prepare an installable iPhone silent-blocking probe
tasks.description:
CURRENT STATE: reuse tools/entry-limit-harness/, not the unfinished production iOS app. CallDir/CallDirectoryHandler.swift:20 loads synthetic consecutive entries to measure capacity; App/App.swift:42 runs/retries reloads and appends timing results; project.yml configures the signed extension; run.sh:12/:15 selects a fixed old device for build/install. apps/ios/CallDirectoryExtension/CallDirectoryHandler.swift:10 only links coreVersion and emits no blocking entries. Existing Release/ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO, NSExtension configuration and incremental-clear fixes must be preserved.

GOAL: an installable, minimal Call Directory probe for the T019 protocol, with one configured real exact number, positive-control/empty-list mode and visible loading/enablement diagnostics. Preserve the historical capacity and identification test modes; do not replace their measured evidence. This probe tests OS blocking behavior, not a shipped editor, number normalization, geographic expansion or complete F004 integration.

IMPLEMENTATION SURFACE: extend tools/entry-limit-harness/{App/App.swift,CallDir/CallDirectoryHandler.swift,project.yml,run.sh,README.md}, with fixture/run helpers under tools/device-tests/ if needed. Select the device explicitly via an argument or environment/configuration input, never a committed UDID or the first of multiple attached devices. Supply already validated canonical exact-number fixtures as private runtime/bundled data, not country-specific source literals. Use the existing Rust core/tooling if rule interpretation or normalization is needed; add no filtering algorithm in Swift.

Provide a real-number blocking mode and an empty/clear control. Honor strictly ascending entries and incremental requests; report reload errors and actual extension enabled/disabled/unknown state. A generated fixture and explicit rebuild/reload is sufficient to change the test entry: do not make App Groups, a paid team or the full production rule store prerequisites merely to share editable test data. Keep signing configuration external and explain any provisioning constraint found.

CHECKS: build for physical iPhone, preserve known build fixes, verify fixture packaging and the empty/nonempty request paths where automation is possible. Prepare reproducible install, enable, clear/disable and cleanup instructions. A device connection may still be required for pairing/provisioning/trust; document this instead of claiming it tested. Never create notifications, caller-ID labels or fake blocked-call history in the new mode. Reload success is only proof that iOS accepted the list. Stop at a preparation-ready report; actual calls and physical acceptance belong to P017.

tasks.title: Prepare an installable Android silent-blocking probe
tasks.description:
CURRENT STATE: apps/android/app/src/main/java/com/antoniopantano/callerfilter/MainActivity.kt:9 displays core version only; apps/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:1 declares no CallScreeningService. apps/android/app/build.gradle.kts:1 already includes generated UniFFI Kotlin/JNI outputs and JNA. tools/build-android.sh:30 cross-compiles the Rust core through cargo-ndk, then generates fresh host-derived bindings. core/src/ffi.rs:309 provides PreparedRules and existing exact-number matching; no new rule type is needed. P001/T002 confirms SDK contracts, not a running device service.

GOAL: use the Android skeleton as a small diagnostic probe for T019, not a full P011/P013 implementation. Add a properly declared CallScreeningService protected by BIND_SCREENING_SERVICE and a minimal role/fixture/status control surface. Proposed files: MainActivity.kt and a new sibling ScreeningService.kt, AndroidManifest.xml, focused tests, tools/device-tests/ run instructions/helper, and build wiring only if required for actual native packaging.

IMPLEMENTATION: request/detect ROLE_CALL_SCREENING; load one user-supplied canonical exact deny rule through the existing Rust PreparedRules boundary, keep number matching in Rust, and adapt its verdict to the OS response. No Kotlin copy of matcher/normalization logic. Keep heavy dataset loading off the call path; the exact-number probe does not require geographic datasets, national-pattern authoring or a whole expansion list. Reply inside the documented five-second screening deadline. Handle nonmatching callers normally and report malformed fixture/unavailable core states honestly rather than accidentally blocking every caller.

For a denied call request blocking and suppression of the missed-call notification, and explicitly document the chosen reject behavior. setSilenceCall alone is insufficient because it can still surface the call UI. Do not launch an overlay or publish a blocked-call notification. Do not rely on setSkipCallLog: current Android documentation says it is ignored for ordinary third-party screening apps, and the user permits call records. Do not request default-dialer/default-SMS status, call-log access or READ_CONTACTS merely for this probe. Explicit numbered callers outside contacts are the baseline.

DIAGNOSTICS: collect local/redacted invocation, core-verdict and response-timing evidence without user-visible notifications. Provide empty-rule/nonmatching controls and a way to clear the fixture. Verify role state at launch/resume and distinguish revoked/not-granted states.

BUILD: verify SDK/NDK/cargo-ndk availability, generate fresh bindings/native libraries with tools/build-android.sh and produce an APK with the required ABI; host Kotlin/JNA tests alone do not prove mobile packaging. Avoid modifying unrelated Gradle/build contracts or exported Rust APIs. Use explicit device selection in install/log instructions and keep personal fixture values and generated outputs ignored. Stop at preparation-ready; runtime role acquisition, real calls and no-disturbance acceptance require P017.

COMPLETED — Android silent-blocking probe HOST PREPARATION only; physical acceptance is not established.

No overlay, app notification, silence-only shortcut, default-dialer/default-SMS role, contacts or call-log permission. MainActivity.kt:17 supplies role request/status, exact-deny, empty-control and recovery controls. ProbeEngine.kt:49/:63 delegates matching exclusively to existing PreparedRules/evaluateNumber; no Rust API changes or Kotlin matcher. ProbeStore.kt:32/:76/:96 serializes initialization/evaluation/preferences off the callback thread and binds persisted activation to fixture identity. Invalid fixture/core/handle/role and late responses permit calls rather than creating blanket blocks. ProbeResponseGate at ProbeEngine.kt:79 prevents duplicate/late responses; the 3000ms resource-configured watchdog is a local setting, not a measured device deadline guarantee.

DIAGNOSTICS: ProbeDiagnostics.kt records redacted request/reason/rule/flags/timing evidence, not call history or proof of framework acceptance. First-request local bind timing is distinguished from reused bindings and unobserved earlier startup. Native handles/data initialization stay off the callback thread. Consent-based fixture values, generated assets, APKs and evidence stay ignored/private. Clearing deny does not erase the number bundled in an exact-fixture APK; docs explain empty rebuild/uninstall only with consent.

BUILD: tools/build-android.sh and tools/uniffi-android.toml regenerate bindings with UniFFI 0.32 global-config syntax and supported JNA cleanup without raising minSdk or patching generated sources. JNA 5.17 fixes x86_64 16KB alignment; ABI filters advertise only arm64-v8a/armeabi-v7a/x86_64 with both Rust and JNA libraries. Gradle requires generated inputs and includes the private asset. Manifest/backup resources disable backup and data transfer. tools/device-tests/android-probe.py:76/:116/:157 separates verified builds from explicitly selected-device installation/log capture. android-probe.md and README.md document prerequisites, controls, capture, cleanup and limitations.

Lint has 0 errors and 10 non-blocking warnings (dependency updates, prototype icon/English text, KTX and a legacy-backup recommendation despite allowBackup=false); no API-level or alignment errors remain. Signature, asset identity, protected service/DEX inventory, paired ABI set, forbidden permissions, ZIP and ELF64 16KB alignment passed. Six final Python tests passed in /tmp/caller-filter-t021-tools-final.log, including a static source-level role/redaction regression guard added after the APK gate; no application code changed afterward.
